version.changelog:
- Added references/mcp.md as the authoritative source for execution, preflight, and verification steps.
- Updated SKILL.md to clarify product scope, behavior, and install rules; user and installer should strictly follow references/mcp.md for workflow.
- SKILL.md description reworded for clearer trigger phrases and purpose.
- No changes to install script or user-facing flow; installer workflow and config merge/check logic are now separated for maintainability.

llm.summary: The installer has a legitimate Gate setup purpose, but it makes broad persistent Cursor changes and pulls mutable remote code/instructions without enough safeguards.

dimensions.detail: Writing Cursor MCP config and skills is expected for this installer, but the default all-services/all-skills install is broad and includes remote MCP endpoints, OAuth flows, and optional trading API credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer clones the mutable master branch of gate-skills, copies all remote skill directories by default, may use unpinned npx gate-mcp, and deletes same-named existing skills before replacement.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to read a mutable GitHub runtime-rules file and treat it as highest priority, leaving part of the effective instruction set outside the reviewed package.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists MCP entries, installed skills, a shared DEX x-api-key value, and optionally user Gate API credentials in mcp.json without strong confirmation, backup, rollback, or file-permission controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent for installing Gate MCP services and skills in Cursor, including trading-related tools, but it handles high-impact trading credentials and persistent agent integrations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Prefer selecting only the MCPs you need and using --no-skills unless you intend to install all Gate skills. Do not enter high-privilege trading API keys unless you accept plaintext storage in Cursor config; use limited, IP-restricted keys where possible. Pin or review the exact gate-mcp version and gate-skills commit before running the installer.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: Accepted: the mutable external rules file is not necessary for a local installer and creates an under-reviewed instruction source.
[T03] expected: Partly accepted: remote installation is part of the stated purpose, but the artifact uses mutable/unpinned sources without integrity verification.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: merge-mcp-config.js treats read or parse failure as an empty config, so malformed existing Cursor config can be overwritten despite the local rule to abort.
[T09] expected: Accepted in context: trading credentials are purpose-related and optional, but the installer can store them persistently in plaintext without enforcing owner-only permissions.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded to a note: the fixed DEX x-api-key is disclosed and may be a public client value, but its privileges are not clearly documented.
[RP1] expected: Accepted as a supply-chain concern: npx gate-mcp is unpinned, so future package changes can affect local execution.
[RA2] expected: Accepted as a persistence concern: Cursor config and skills directory changes are expected, but they persist into future sessions and default to a broad install.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: existing same-named skill directories are removed before replacement with no backup or explicit confirmation.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: api.gatemcp.ai endpoints are clearly listed as Gate remote MCP services, and the artifact does not show hidden exfiltration.
[EA1] unexpected: Not accepted as stated: the artifact limits MCP business tools, but the separate mutable external-rules instruction remains a real scope concern.
[EA2] unexpected: Not accepted: the cited text requires verification before claiming success rather than authorizing autonomous high-impact action.
